WarTranslated Monitoring channels say a cruise missile crossed into Polish airspace this morning. Poland's army says it got word of a suspected violation by unidentified air objects and is now checking radar data. Poland's Operational Command says an object probably came down near Chmielek in Bilgoraj county, PAP reports. Online reports say CCTV caught an explosion there, about 46 km from the Ukrainian border. Polish authorities have not officially reported it. Tusk says he received reports from ministers Kosiniak-Kamysz and Kierwinski. There is no air threat for now, and services are working at the site, he says. tweet

Nuno Felix RT @ChrisRMcGuire : The @HouseForeignGOP just released information about all AI chip shipments that @CommerceGov approved to China, which calls into question whether Commerce was conducting any real national security reviews of AI chip shipments to China, or if it just outsourced that review to Nvidia as well. As of May 11, 2026, @BISgov had approved the shipment of nearly 900,000 Nvidia H200 or AMD MI325X AI chips to China. Over 30% of these chips were sent to companies that the Department of War has designated as Chinese Military Companies. And remarkably, every license application from Nvidia and AMD said the shipment posed a "low" risk of diversion. There is simply no way that the Department of Commerce did a serious national security review of these licenses. Also, yesterday @jingyanghk reported in @theinformation that Commerce approved some H200 licenses over the objections of the Departments of State, Energy, and War, and that Commerce claimed that the legally mandated interagency review process (which requires at least three of those four agencies to support granting a license before it can be approved) was not needed for H200 chips and it could approve these licenses unilaterally. These chips were shipped to companies that the Trump administration itself has designated as Chinese Military Companies, but somehow the shipments pose a "low" risk of diversion? @BISgov just took Nvidia's word for it that the shipments posed no risk, potentially over the objection of the entire US national security apparatus. Even the people who support sending AI chips to China cannot possibly defend shipping chips to designated Chinese Military Companies. Just more evidence that Commerce has completely abdicated its responsibilities on export controls. https://foreignaffairs.house.gov/news/press-releases/chairman-brian-mast-exercises-legislative-authority-to-publicly-release-ai-chip-license-information-for-china tweet
